rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nepal's vegetation stacks six climate zones up its slopes: tropical sal and sissoo forests below 1000 m; subtropical chir pine with Schima and Castanopsis from 1000–2000 m; temperate oak, blue pine, fir, hemlock and rhododendron from 2000–3000 m; subalpine birch and juniper to 4000 m; alpine Kobresia meadows and cushion plants to 5000 m; and the nival snowline beyond, where only lichens persist.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Vegetation = natural plant cover; determined by climate + altitude + soil + human activity
Types in Nepal: Terai → Sub-montane → Temperate → Sub-alpine → Alpine → Nival
In-situ: protected areas + community forests + sacred groves

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Chir pine vs blue pine:** Pinus roxburghii = subtropical (1000–2000 m); Pinus wallichiana = temperate (2000–3000 m+).  ·  **Bhabar vs Terai:** Bhabar = porous boulder belt with deep water table; Terai = fertile alluvial plain with sal and grasslands.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the definition of vegetation and its determinants (climate, altitude, soil, human activity).  ·  List Nepal's vegetation types by altitude.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Shorea robusta*** — sal; the Terai's timber giant.  ·  ***Rhododendron arboreum*** — lali gurans, Nepal's national flower, of the temperate zone.

rows.text: "Sal below, pine middle, oak-fir higher, birch then meadow, then snow."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m): Name the tree line altitude in Nepal and what grows above it.** — The tree line lies at ~4000 m; above it grow alpine meadows (Kobresia, primulas), cushion plants and dwarf juniper–rhododendron shrubs, with only lichens and mosses above ~5000 m.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: zones by altitude (2023, 2024), deciduous vs evergreen (2024), sal (2024), Terai/Bhabar (2022).  ·  Diagram-worthy: altitudinal zonation profile of Nepal (mountain cross-section with zone bands).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Altitude mirrors latitude:** climbing 1000 m ≈ moving 1000 km poleward — Nepal's vertical gradient is a continent of climates in 200 km.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Six zones: tropical (<1000 m sal, sissoo), subtropical (1000–2000 m chir pine, Schima), temperate (2000–3000 m oak, blue pine, fir, rhododendron), subalpine (3000–4000 m birch, juniper), alpine (4000–5000 m Kobresia meadows, cushion plants), nival (>5000 m lichens only).  ·  Temperature falls ~6 °C per 1000 m — the zonation driver.  ·  Sal = tropical deciduous dominant; uses: timber, resin, seed oil.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nepal holds about 2% of the world's flowering plant species on 0.1% of its land — a direct consequence of this vertical zonation.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Nepal as a Vertical Garden Nepal compresses five climatic zones from the Terai plains (below 300 m) to the nival zone above 5000 m — a vertical gradient that packs vegetation from sal forests to alpine meadows within 200 km. This altitudinal zonation is the syllabus's core: know each zone's altitude range, dominant species and character.  ·  ## 2. Vegetation Zones of Nepal by Altitude (NEB 2023 & 2024) | Zone | Altitude | Vegetation | Typical species | |---|---|---|---| | **1. Tropical zone** | Below ~1000 m (Terai, Siwaliks, Bhabar, low valleys) | Tropical deciduous and evergreen forest | **Sal (*Shorea robusta*)**, sissoo (*Dalbergia sissoo*), khair (*Acacia catechu*), simal (*Bombax ceiba*), Terminalia;…  ·  ## 3. Factors Controlling This Zonation | Factor | Gradient | Effect | |---|---|---| | **Temperature** | Falls ~6 °C per 1000 m | The master variable — mirrors latitude vertically | | Rainfall | High monsoon mid-hills; rain-shadow (Mustang, Manang) dry | Deciduous vs evergreen vs xeric vegetation | | Altitude (atmospheric pressure, UV) | Thin air, intense UV at height | Dwarf,…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ex-situ: botanical gardens + seed banks + tissue culture + herbaria  ·  Human impact: jhum + grazing + firewood + logging + climate change + pollution  ·  **Alpine vs nival:** alpine (4000–5000 m) has meadows and cushion plants; nival (5000 m+) is essentially beyond plants.
